Introduction

BI users need to compare several matrix and choice questions and apply their own scoring logic in one consistent view.

​

Advanced Heatmap combines answer distributions and segment comparisons, with configurable custom metrics, filters and answer labels.

3 of 16

Problems

One workflow, two analysis models

Matrix Heatmap provides answer distributions for one matrix. Heat Map Chart supports several questions but displays means for respondent segments. Users need both analyses across mixed questions without confusing answer options with respondent groups.

​

​

4 of 16

Scope

Supported: 1–25 matrix or choice questions from one survey, all with the same number of answer options.
Analysis: Answer distribution and Segment comparison, switchable after creation.
Controls: custom metrics, result filters, answer labels, live preview and regular Heat Map segment controls.
Deferred: label merging and base selector; unsupported types, cross-survey analysis and cross-chart metric reuse.
Existing heatmap widgets remain unchanged.

5 of 16
Select up to 25 whole matrices and choice questions with matching option counts.
Choose Answer distribution or Segment comparison; switch later in Analytics.
Add a named custom metric with editable original-answer weights.
Rename, reorder or exclude answer labels; filter and preview results.
Use the standard widget header, three-dot menu and settings panel.

​

Solution

6 of 16

Prototype walkthrough

Open https://survey-re.vercel.app/ → Dashboards → open a dashboard.
Inspect the default Advanced Heatmap, or choose Add widget → Advanced widgets → Advanced Heatmap.
Select Next → survey → 1–25 questions with equal option counts → Next.
Choose Answer distribution or Segment comparison → Create widget.
Open ⋮ → Settings. Configure General, Analytics, Labels and Design while previewing results.
Apply to commit; Cancel or close to discard. Switch analysis in Analytics to compare both views.

7 of 16

Selection rules

Question selection and display

Select 1–25 supported questions from one survey; a whole matrix counts as one.
All questions must have the same original option count; matrix row counts may differ.
Keep name, type, checkbox, search and step checkpoints. Creation counter always shows “X out of 25”.
In creation and Labels, tooltips explain unsupported types, option-count mismatches and the 25-question limit. Keep selected questions removable.
Changing survey clears selection; Next/Create/Apply require valid choices. Matrices expand to show statements.

8 of 16

Answer distribution rules

Columns follow original answer positions; column count equals the shared option count.
Unequal option counts cannot be combined. Equal counts do not imply equivalent labels or weights.
Choose counts or percentages; use a fixed valid-respondent base. No base selector.
Multi-select respondent percentages can exceed 100%; empty cells remain neutral.
Matrix summaries pool valid statement answers; never average row means.

9 of 16

Segment comparison rules

Columns are selectable respondent segments; create, rename, edit or remove named AND/OR groups.
Each row averages that segment’s valid answers. Retain Overall, response counts and overall average.
Retain 0–4 decimals, Default/0–5/0–10 mean ranges and independent question reversal.
Retain 2–5 threshold bands, editable cutoffs and response statistics; overlapping segments are not additive.
Custom metrics keep their own scale. Nominal answers require weights; code averages are not ratings.

10 of 16

Custom metrics

Off by default: column hidden, weights blank; name editable in Analytics.
Every included original answer needs a finite weight; missing weights block Apply.
Single-select/matrices: sum(count × weight) ÷ valid answers, using Matrix Heatmap weight logic.
Multi-select: mean selected weights per respondent, then mean respondents.
Distribution adds a metric column; Segment comparison scores each segment’s paired answers.
Omit missing/excluded answers. Empty bases show unavailable; reverse = min + max − weight.

11 of 16

Filter by custom metric

General → Filter type → Custom Metric; enabled only after applying a valid metric in Answer distribution. Disabled items use a not-allowed cursor.
Keep condition and threshold fields on one row. Compare unrounded scores: below, at most, above, at least or inclusive between.
Accept finite decimals, including negative values; reject blank thresholds or reversed ranges.
Hide result rows, not respondents; bases and matrix totals remain unchanged.
Test parents and children independently; keep a context-only parent when a child passes.
Missing scores never match. Show condition, matching count, Clear filter and no-results state.
Switching to segments or removing the metric disables this filter. Retain thresholds; reselect Custom Metric to reactivate. Re-evaluate changed weights/exclusions.

12 of 16

Answer labels

Answer-level controls

Rename, reorder and exclude answer labels only. Label merging is deferred.
Keep all questions and search in a scrollable Labels dropdown. Omit selection instruction banners in creation and Labels; show types without “Unavailable” text.
Preserve original-answer IDs and weights when labels are renamed or reordered.
Multi-select percentages use respondents answering the row; totals may exceed 100%.
Excluded answers leave the valid base and metric. Exclusion does not change selection eligibility.

13 of 16
Open ⋮ → Settings for an enlarged live preview beside the standard panel.
General: Dashboard, Widget, Combined, None or Custom Metric. Respondent filters apply before calculations; metric filters hide calculated rows.
Analytics: switch analysis; retain regular Heat Map controls and configure Custom metrics.
Labels: select questions; manage answer labels in Distribution and segments in Segment comparison.
Apply commits changes; Cancel or close discards them. Mode switches preserve configuration.

Settings and filters

14 of 16

Worked example

Custom metric on a 0–100 scale

Answer counts: Poor 30, Average 33, Good 25, Excellent 24; valid base = 112.
Weights 0, 0, 100, 100 → (25 + 24) × 100 ÷ 112 = 43.75 (display 43.8).
Exclude Poor → 49 × 100 ÷ 82 = 59.7561 (display 59.8).
Rename Good or Excellent → labels change; the custom metric remains unchanged.
Filter “at least 80” hides this row; “below 80” retains it. Use the unrounded score.

15 of 16

Acceptance criteria

Functional and calculation acceptance

Allow 1–25 questions with equal option counts in both modes; block a 26th or mismatched choice.
Counts, percentages, weights, pooled totals and segment controls match calculation tests; no merge/base selector.
Exact filter boundaries, missing scores and no results behave as specified; matching children remain reachable.
Matrices count once despite differing row counts. Creation, Labels, Apply and Cancel enforce both rules.
Verify fixed “X out of 25”, reason tooltips, clean type labels and no instruction banners. Native controls and widget styling match existing widgets.

16 of 16

Review and acceptance

Advanced Heatmap review checklist

Open Survey-RE directly: https://survey-re.vercel.app/
Follow the Prototype walkthrough to review Advanced Heatmap.
Review source selection, row/column mappings, metric configuration and filter behavior.
Confirm weighting, date/status/system filters, configuration persistence, source editing and exports against the requirements.
Validate calculations and access rules against the acceptance criteria.
